contributions.head: f2d83999edccdad625ea686ff3f0d03b7d208965
contributions.title: Prove exact two-call capacity for homogeneous query chains (no new κ)
contributions.claim_excerpt:
The conditional three-field controller in #4698 leaves open how much useful work two homogeneous chain calls can deliver. This package proves and attains the exact capacity **r = 2 floor((n-1)/2)** for every chain length n >= 2 in the explicitly restricted scalar/global-P ring, where P=Q^2. It includes an all-odd construction and a separate weighted cyclic middle boundary attaining n-2 jobs for every even n. Both restore all arbitrary spectator inputs. The matching rank/parity proof allows arbitrary restored dirty workspace, arbitrary invertible boundaries in that ring, and either inverse/transpose orientation.

The explicit reversible boundaries have linear field-macro counts. The proof states Q^T=Q, Q^4=I and the faithful-width restriction for the upper bound; it does not extend that bound to arbitrary physical address/monomial operations or every isolated small width. The three-field identity, native lineage and source attribution remain credited to #4698 and its predecessors.

The complete conditional moment is `2 H_t + r(2b+1)^t + (n-r)(2b)^t - 2 P_t`. Direct synthesis from n-1 unary queries loses at least `2(n-1)-r` moment units throughout `0<=t<=1`, even with favorable transverse pricing. Physical chain acquisition, actual charts, helper autonomy/restoration, movement/precision, completion, compiler, BIT and outer funding remain unresolved. **No native supplier, new kappa, selected-frontier change or full multiplication theorem is claimed.** The next physical gate is a named positive complete provider invoice; the package stops direct unary synthesis.

contributions.head: 6779a28938a9af1ba3d32e18ba8feb8d7cc002f8
contributions.title: Prove eight bits are necessary for algebra-faithful affine A5 actions
contributions.claim_excerpt:
Nick Petalas's #5114 constructs an algebra-faithful A5 action on eight binary address bits and leaves the minimum over all affine representations open. This proves **eight is the minimum**, including nonsplit representations and affine actions without a fixed point. It answers that PR's Open next question 2; its eight-bit upper construction retains full credit.

The new reduction covers every relevant module, rather than sampling smaller candidates. An exact quotient of F2[A5] identifies all simple modules (dimensions 1, 4, 4), with kernel powers of dimensions `35,27,17,9,0`. Every module with one nontrivial composition factor is a subquotient of one of two explicit universal eight-dimensional extensions, plus fixed summands. Their actions on all 256 vectors have algebra ranks **52 and 34**, with explicit nonzero annihilators. An affine action on at most seven bits homogenizes to a module of dimension at most eight with a trivial quotient, so it falls under this obstruction. The written proof includes the nonsplit, subquotient and affine-slice steps.

Only seven files in `research/a5-affine-address-minimum/` are added. The complete proof is in its README; the finite quotient has a separately implemented checker. Both implementations explicitly reconcile their natural-module coordinate bases.
